title: Green passes Wickens to win Lausitzring Race 2 as Audi takes five of the top seven
dek: Jamie Green passed pole-sitter Robert Wickens on lap 31 to win DTM Race 2 at the Lausitzring by 6.295 seconds, with Audi team-mate Mattias Ekström second after stopping on lap one.

chapters.title: Auer's lead after a Saturday of Mercedes strength
text: Saturday had gone to Mercedes. Lucas Auer won Race 1 from pole, Robert Wickens, pointless at Hockenheim, finished second, and the Austrian left the day with a 34-point lead over team-mate Gary Paffett. Audi's best moment was René Rast's third place, his first DTM podium, while Jamie Green, excluded from qualifying for a wrongly allocated tyre, had fought from last on the grid to tenth. Sunday's race was another with a free choice of when to make the mandatory stop, and the Saturday results had shown that the early stoppers could make up ground.

chapters.title: Wickens takes pole as the leader falls to 15th
text: Sunday's qualifying was tighter still. Many drivers fitted new tyres with seven minutes left, using the first flying lap to warm them, and the order was settled in the last three minutes. Tom Blomqvist went fastest in the #31 BMW with 1m16.323s, and Green completed his lap just 0.003 seconds slower. Wickens then took pole with 1m16.299s, 0.024 seconds ahead of Blomqvist, his first pole of the season.

Green's Audi was third on the grid. Paffett in the second Mercedes was fourth, 0.069 seconds off pole, with Maxime Martin fifth, 0.080 behind, and Rast, Nico Müller and Mattias Ekström in sixth to eighth. Augusto Farfus and Marco Wittmann completed the top ten, with the reigning champion 0.280 seconds off the pace.

Saturday's winner Auer could only manage 15th, 0.513 seconds from pole, and led a group of four Mercedes drivers at the back of the field with Paul di Resta, Maro Engel and Edoardo Mortara. Mortara was last of the 18 cars.

chapters.title: Ekström and Rockenfeller stop on lap one
text: Wickens converted pole into the lead at the start. Blomqvist held second at first but had jumped the start and was given a five-second penalty, and he slipped back, with Green passing him on lap four and Paffett following through. Blomqvist faded after his stop and finished 17th.

The strategic gamble came from the Audis. Rockenfeller and Ekström both pitted at the end of the first lap, Ekström from eighth on the grid and Rockenfeller from eleventh. On fresh tyres they began to carry speed that the cars in front could not match. Auer, already up to ninth from 15th on the grid, was held up behind Farfus and pitted on lap 12.

chapters.title: Green stops a lap after Wickens and closes in
text: Paffett was the first of the leading group to stop, around lap 13, and Ekström went past him on his new tyres on the way to the front. Wickens came in next, and Green a lap after him. Green briefly led the race on the road, but Wickens had warmer tyres and took the place back.

Wickens said afterwards that stopping on the first lap had not been possible for the Mercedes, because the tyres would not have lasted, and that the team chose a relatively early stop because of Ekström's pace. Once the stops were done he led again, but Green was within a second and stayed there for several laps. On lap 31 Green passed him for the lead and then pulled out of DRS range so that Wickens could not hit back on the following lap.

chapters.title: Ekström takes second from Wickens, Green wins by 6.3 seconds
text: Green pulled away in clear air and won in 56m20.480s, 6.295 seconds ahead of Ekström, for his second win of the season. Ekström had run 42 laps on his second set of tyres, and he sat behind Wickens for seven laps, saving his DRS, before passing him on lap 38 to take second.

Wickens held third, 7.034 seconds from the winner, with Paffett 0.353 seconds behind him in fourth. Rockenfeller climbed from eleventh to fifth on the same strategy as Ekström, Müller was sixth and Rast seventh, and five Audis finished in the top seven. Rast also set the fastest lap, 1m17.098s on lap 25.
BMW had a difficult day: Martin was eighth and Wittmann ninth, the only points for the brand. Auer recovered from 15th on the grid to finish tenth and take one point.

chapters.title: Auer's lead cut to 16 points by Green
text: Green said the Audi's early tyre change had been the key, because otherwise he would probably have been stuck behind Wickens. He also said that qualifying remained difficult for Audi, but that the races were working better, which he called good for entertainment. Ekström said his lap-one stop had carried no risk, and that he could have run another 20 laps on the same set of Hankook tyres.

Wickens, who had left Hockenheim without a point, took two podiums and a pole from the weekend. He had hoped for more after taking pole, he said, but admitted that Audi had been very fast in the second stint and that he had been unable to answer. He added that the championship was only just getting started for him. Mercedes' DTM head Ulrich Fritz said it was a pity the pole could not be converted into a win, but that the team could be satisfied. Wittmann said BMW still lacked something compared with the Audis and needed to better understand how the Hankook tyre worked with its package.

The weekend left a clear split between the brands. Mercedes had taken a one-two and five top-ten places on Saturday, while Audi's tyre strategy won Sunday and put five cars in the top seven. BMW's best result was Martin's fourth place in Race 1, and Blomqvist's front-row start in Race 2 ended with a false-start penalty and 17th place.

In the championship, Auer's single point from Sunday took him to 69. Green's win moved him back up to second on 53 points, 16 behind the Mercedes driver, with each of them now holding two victories from the first four races. Green said there was still a long way to go to the final race but that things were going well for the moment. Auer called it a great weekend for the team overall, even if his speed in the second race was perhaps not outstanding. The DTM travels next to the Hungaroring, near Budapest, on 17 and 18 June.

facts.v: Jamie Green won in 56m20.480s, 6.295 seconds ahead of Mattias Ekström, passing Robert Wickens for the lead on lap 31.
